items.title: Systemic failures and insider threats: Reassessing airport security
items.summary: THE article by Sharanjit Singh in NST yesterday (Aug 11, 2026) is commendable for its insightful and timely examination of Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) security issues. Such thoughtful analysis contributes meaningfully to public discourse on national security and border management in Malaysia. The concerns surrounding security at KLIA deserve to be examined beyond the immediate question of whether airport scanners are sufficiently modern or whether individual officers have performed their duties properly.

items.title: Woman charged with operating RM1.7mil kootu scheme
items.summary: ALOR STAR: A woman was charged in the Sessions Court today with organising a tontine (kootu) scheme involving more than RM1.7 million since last year. Siti Zulaika Ahmad Sabri, 36, pleaded guilty after the charge was read before judge Sharmila Abdul Samad. According to the charge, she organised the scheme involving 52 participants who made cash payments into the fund between July 2025 and July this year at a house in Kampung Padang Satu, Bukit Kayu Hitam, Changlun.

items.title: Johor to cancel housing approvals if developers delay affordable homes
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: Johor will cancel housing project approvals if developers fail to meet agreed deadlines for their affordable housing commitments. Johor Housing and Local Government Committee chairman Datuk Mohd Jafni Md Shukor said affordable housing components must not lag behind open-market developments. "Open-market housing and RMMJ must move in tandem.

items.title: Customs foils bid to hide RM650,000 worth of cannabis in rubbish heap
items.summary: KANGAR: A drug syndicate's attempt to hide a sack containing more than 8kg of cannabis in a rubbish heap was foiled by the Perlis Customs Department. Perlis Customs director Mohammad Furiman Hattar said the seizure of 8.123kg of cannabis flowers, worth RM649,840, was among six enforcement operations conducted by the department this year. Furiman said the department also foiled four other smuggling attempts involving cigarettes, gas stoves and liquor.

items.title: Taiwan condemns China's plan for navy drill with Indonesia off island's east
items.summary: TAIPEI, Aug 12 — Taiwan has condemned China’s plan to hold a navy drill with Indonesia this month off the democratic island’s east coast, saying Beijing seeks to create the “false impression” that it has jurisdiction over the area. China claims Taiwan is part of its territory and insists it has authority over the waters surrounding the island, which Taipei rejects. Taiwan’s top China policy body hit back late yesterday, saying it “strongly condemned the CCP military provocation”, referring to the Chinese Communist Party.

items.title: Bangladeshi man charged with murder of three compatriots
items.summary: However, the magistrate ruled that a foreign language interpreter be called to re-read the charges after observing that the accused had difficulty understanding Bahasa Malaysia. "All three charges were read to the accused. According to the charges, the accused allegedly murdered Md Nozrul Islam, Mohasin, and Kiron Miah.

items.title: MCBA warns firms over fake procurement documents using DG's identity
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (MCBA) has warned companies to be wary of fraudulent government procurement documents bearing the signature of its director-general (DG). The agency said it had received complaints from companies that were sent documents purportedly issued as Letters of Acceptance for government procurement exercises. MCBA said that all its procurement matters were conducted in accordance with existing government procurement procedures, regulations and rules.

items.title: Police cripple housebreaking syndicate with arrest of five Chinese citizens
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Police have crippled a housebreaking syndicate following the arrest of five men from China during two raids in Sri Petaling and Pudu. "Acting on information and intelligence, police carried out two raids in Sri Petaling and Pudu at 9.30pm on Aug 9. Fadil said police also recovered items belonging to the complainant during the raids.

items.title: Rosmah must secure RM67.5m or face enforcement, says Global Royalty
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Lebanese jewellery company Global Royalty Trading SAL says its RM67.5 million judgment against Datin Seri Rosmah Mansor remains protected whether she complies with the High Court's condition for a stay pending her appeal or not. The senior lawyer said the money would remain secured in the account pending the outcome of Rosmah's appeal at the Court of Appeal. He said if Rosmah failed to deposit the full amount within the 30-day period, Global Royalty would be entitled to proceed with execution of the judgment.

items.title: Police seek Indonesian man over Banting plantation murder
items.summary: KUALA LANGAT: Police are seeking an Indonesian man believed to have information that could assist investigations into the murder of a 49-year-old man at an oil palm plantation in Banting. Kuala Langat police chief Superintendent Mohd Akmalrizal Radzi said the man, known as "Balancing", was being sought as a witness in the investigation. The latest development comes after police arrested eight people in connection with the case.

items.title: Multi-layered security strategy needed for more secure borders
items.summary: They use commercial flights, cargo routes, fishing boats, tankers, hidden road compartments and illegal border crossings. Other cases show how syndicates recruit vulnerable people. In Johor, also in July, police arrested eight people, including a 16-year-old alleged drug transporter, and seized drugs worth RM3.04 million.

items.title: Govt urged to let 15th Parliament complete full term
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The government has been urged to ensure the 15th Parliament completes its full term until Dec 18 next year, unless it loses the confidence of the House. They said the government should allow parliament to complete its full term to realise as many reforms as possible to strengthen democracy and improve good governance. "Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim should convene a cross-party leaders' summit involving all government and opposition parties represented in parliament to establish a common agenda for the remaining term of the 15th Parliament.

items.title: Six schools in Sarawak shift to online learning as haze hits ‘very unhealthy’ levels
items.summary: The Sarawak Education Department (JPNS) said the precautionary measure was taken in line with the Education Ministry’s (MOE) guidelines, with the safety, health and wellbeing of students and school staff given priority. As of 10.30am today, the schools involved are SK Sejijag, with 51 students and 14 staff; SK Sungai Sameran (129 students, 21 staff); SK Tepoi (42 students, 15 staff); SK Entubuh (67 students, 18 staff); SK Temong (205 students, 21 staff); and SK Tema (85 students, 15 staff). According to JPNS, these schools are under the administration of the Serian District Education Office (Serian PPD).

items.title: Lar gibbon linked to Indian actor Vikram traced to Malaysia
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A lar gibbon at the centre of an investigation involving Indian actor Vikram has been traced to Malaysia, with records listing the country as its place of origin. The Hindu reported that Chennai Wildlife Warden Yogesh Kulal said the gibbon had since been moved to Erode, India, from businessman C.K. Erode district forest officer K.V.

items.title: Wong Chen apologises for quitting early, stands by his 13-year-record
items.summary: PUCHONG: Former Subang MP Wong Chen said today he was not apologising for his years of service as an elected representative, but for stepping down a year before the next general election. "No, I am not apologising for resigning. "Resigning one year early is the apology I give to the people.

items.title: One of two boys missing after river dip in Kuala Krai found dead, search continues for second 14-year-old (VIDEO)
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Aug 12 — The body of one of two 14-year-old boys who went missing while bathing in a river in Kampung Batu Lada, Aur Duri, Kuala Krai, yesterday was found today. The body of Luth Naiman Mohd Noraziron was found by members of the Water Rescue Team (PPDA) of the Kelantan Fire and Rescue Department at 9.10 am, about 100 metres from the incident site. It said today’s operation involved 56 personnel from the JBPM, police, Volunteer Fire Brigades and local residents.

items.title: Situation in West Bank requires urgent action: UN envoy
items.summary: NEW YORK: The situation in the West Bank must be treated as an emergency requiring urgent action, said a United Nations (UN) envoy on Tuesday, reported Xinhua. Israeli monitoring organisations report that agricultural and pastoral outposts now exercise effective control over close to 20 per cent of the West Bank, he said. "They are reshaping the West Bank, weakening Palestinian governance and advancing de-facto annexation," said the envoy.

items.title: Subsidised cooking oil diverted for used-oil resale, 3,150kg seized
items.summary: BUKIT MERTAJAM: The Penang Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry (KPDN) seized 3,150kg of subsidised packet cooking oil during an integrated Ops Tiris 4.0 raid. Penang KPDN director S. Jegan said the seizure followed a month-long intelligence operation targeting three premises, with a 51-year-old local man detained to assist investigations. He said enforcement officers raided the premises yesterday with about 2,300kg of one-kilogramme packet cooking oil seized at the first two locations and another 850kg found as excess stock at a licensed premises.

items.title: Man with criminal record charged with robbing, injuring Indian citizen
items.summary: Mohd Salim Kapoor Rahim, 40, made the plea after the charge was read before Sessions Court Judge Irwan Suainbon. Deputy public prosecutor Anuarul Hakim Abdul Muen offered RM10,000 bail with additional conditions that the accused report to the police station, refrain from contacting the victim and prosecution witnesses, and surrender his passport to the court. The court allowed bail at RM7,000 with the additional conditions sought by the prosecution.

items.title: Cross-border e-commerce opens global markets for Malaysian MSMEs
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Cross-border e-commerce is emerging as a key gateway for Malaysian micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) to tap global markets, with the eTRADE 2.0 programme generating RM438.7 million in actual export sales. Participating companies have expanded into 163 export markets, including less conventional destinations such as Réunion Island, Kiribati and Nauru, according to findings from the eTRADE 2.0 programme. The programme also contributed to employment creation, with at least 661 jobs generated among participating companies.

items.title: Selangor Rail Line still in planning stage, completion targeted for 2060
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Aug 12 — The Selangor government is still in the discussion stage with various parties including the private sector to identify the appropriate development and financing model for the development of the Selangor Rail Line. State Investment, Trade and Mobility Exco Ng Sze Han said the state government through the Menteri Besar of Selangor (Incorporated) or MBI as the Technical Committee for Selangor Rail Development is examining the most potential development and financing model to be implemented. He said the mechanism for implementing the development of the Selangor Rail Line is also being refined to identify the most profitable and appropriate method.

items.title: MEF urges govt to act faster before MSME cash crunch turns into job losses
items.summary: MEF president Datuk Dr Syed Hussain Syed Husman has proposed that the government consider introducing a coordinated MSME survival and resilience package to help businesses navigate ongoing cost and cash-flow pressures. He said the package should include targeted and temporary tax relief, faster and simpler access to financing and greater use of cash-flow-based lending. “Under this package, the government should consider expanding government-backed guarantees, temporary regulatory and compliance relief, faster payments to MSME suppliers, greater MSME access to government procurement and employment retention support,” he said in a statement today.

items.title: Wong Chen joins Bersama after resigning as Subang MP
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 12 — Former Subang MP Wong Chen has joined Bersama, days after resigning from his parliamentary seat. Wong, a three-term MP who had been with PKR for nearly two decades, had previously indicated that he would eventually leave the party after Rafizi and Nik Nazmi Nik Ahmad resigned their parliamentary seats to lead Bersama. The other two were Ampang MP Rodziah Ismail and Petaling Jaya MP Lee Chean Chung.

items.title: Dr Wan Azizah: Anwar expected to be discharged from hospital today
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim is expected to be discharged from hospital today after receiving treatment, his wife Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail said. She said Anwar expressed his appreciation to everyone who had prayed for his health and well-being. "PMX sends his regards and thanked everyone who has prayed for his health and recovery," she said.

items.title: Waiting for your university offer? UPUOnline results out Aug 14 noon
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 12 — The results of applications for further studies at public universities (UA) via UPUOnline® for the Bachelor’s Degree level for the 2026/2027 Academic Session for STPM/equivalent holders will be announced on August 14. Results can be checked from 12 noon, August 14 to 5 pm, August 23 online via the links https://upu.mohe.gov.my, https://upu2.mohe.gov.my and via the Mobile UPUPocket or Mobile MyGov applications on smartphones. “Only applicants who are unsuccessful in receiving an offer can submit an appeal application via UPUOnline® for admission to UA at https://upu.mohe.gov.my within 10 days from August 14 to 23,” said the Ministry of Education.

items.title: Durian orchard caretaker fined RM7,500 over fake gun, criminal intimidation
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: A durian orchard caretaker was fined RM7,500 by the magistrate's court today after pleading guilty to possessing a fake firearm and criminal intimidation. On the first charge, Choong admitted to unlawfully possessing a fake firearm, a Hatsan AT44-10 QE air rifle bearing serial number 041521754, in his hut at a durian orchard in Bukit Gambir here at 10pm on Aug 5. On the second charge, Choong admitted to criminally intimidating a 42-year-old man by threatening to cause him serious injury at the same durian orchard about 5pm on Aug 4.

items.title: Rwanda to name 22 baby gorillas as conservation, tourism continue to grow
items.summary: KIGALI: Rwanda will name 22 baby mountain gorillas born over the past 12 months on Sept 4 during the 21st edition of the Kwita Izina gorilla-naming ceremony, officials announced on Tuesday, reported Xinhua. Kwita Izina has become a major conservation and tourism event, highlighting Rwanda's efforts to protect mountain gorillas while linking wildlife conservation to tourism, community development and sustainable economic growth. "For over two decades, Kwita Izina has showcased Rwanda's belief that conservation is not simply about protecting wildlife.

items.title: PPA Asia Tour brings world-class pickleball action to KL next month
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: World-class pickleball is set to take centre stage in Kuala Lumpur this September as the Leapmotor Kuala Lumpur Cup 2026 brings five days of Professional Pickleball Association (PPA) Asia Tour action to The Hood. Pickletown will be set up throughout the event, offering food, games, giveaways, exclusive merchandise and activities to complement the tournament atmosphere. Single-day Banger and Dinker GA tickets are also available.

items.title: Wong Chen joins Bersama after quitting PKR
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Former Subang member of parliament Wong Chen today joined Bersama, days after resigning from his parliamentary seat. The announcement was made by Bersama co-leader Datuk Seri Rafizi Ramli at a press conference at the party's headquarters in Puchong today. MORE TO COME © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: Wrong to draw conclusions on TH given RCI's limited scope, says BN's Zambry
items.summary: The Barisan Nasional secretary-general said the RCI's scope was limited to 2014 to 2020, and that developments and decisions made after 2020 should be considered. Commenting on the special parliamentary sitting on the report, Zambry said the report's tabling and subsequent debate by MPs demonstrated transparency in the matter. Zambry said BN had, from the outset, supported the tabling and debate of the RCI report in Parliament.

items.title: Rod Stewart cancels remainder of US tour after heart operation
items.summary: LONDON: British singer Rod Stewart has cancelled the remainder of his 2026 United States (US) tour dates after undergoing heart surgery, reported PA Media/dpa. The 81-year-old singer confirmed on Instagram that he will take four weeks off to recover after undergoing a coronary stent procedure, effectively cutting short his US and Mexico performances, which were due to continue into September. The announcement came after Stewart postponed shows in Cincinnati and Cleveland following medical concerns.

items.title: Kedah fails to overturn ruling against refusal to renew pool betting, lottery licences
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 12 — The Kedah government has failed to overturn a ruling that barred it from refusing to renew licences for pool betting and lottery operators. Free Malaysia Today (FMT) reported that a Federal Court panel chaired by Justice Datuk Rhodzariah Bujang held that the legal questions proposed by the state government failed to meet the threshold for determination by the court. The court also ordered the Kedah government to pay RM50,000 in costs.

items.title: Kelantan sets sights on petroleum, gas opportunities through new state vehicle
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Aug 12 — The Kelantan government intends to strengthen its involvement in the petroleum and gas industry to ensure that the benefits of natural resources can be enjoyed by the people, besides contributing to the state’s sustainable economic development. “In line with the state government’s wishes, the Kelantan Menteri Besar Corporation has established Kelantan Ventures Sdn Bhd (KVSB) as a special purpose company to explore opportunities for participation in the petroleum and gas industry in a more structured and strategic manner. “Through KVSB, Kelantan is building capacity, exploring investment opportunities and establishing collaborations with reputable companies in the industry value chain,” he said.

items.title: SWCorp investigates alleged dumping of Singapore construction waste in Pontian
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: The Solid Waste Management and Public Cleansing Corporation (SWCorp) is investigating the origin of construction and demolition waste allegedly brought from Singapore and dumped at several locations in Pontian. Johor Health and Environment Committee chairman Ling Tian Soon said SWCorp was looking at where the waste came from. Initial checks found that the site was not a gazetted facility for solid waste management, and no permit or approval had been issued for the import or management of construction waste.

items.title: Putrajaya chokes as unhealthy air readings climb across Malaysia
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 12 — Eight areas nationwide recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as at 9 am today, comprising six in Sarawak and two in Peninsular Malaysia. In Peninsular Malaysia, Putrajaya recorded an API reading of 114, while another area also recorded an unhealthy reading of above 100. Meanwhile, 51 areas recorded moderate API readings (51 to 100), and four areas recorded good air quality readings (below 50).

items.title: High Court orders Rosmah to pay RM67.4m into stakeholder account pending appeal in missing jewellery suit
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 12 — Datin Seri Rosmah Mansor was today ordered by the High Court to pay RM67.4 million into a joint stakeholder account within a month, pending her appeal in a suit filed by Lebanese jeweller Global Royalty Trading SAL to recover the value of 43 jewellery items delivered to her. Rosmah had previously sought to stay the execution of the High Court’s June 10 decision, with the court having fixed today to deliver its decision on the application. “In the circumstances, the Court orders that a conditional stay of execution be granted to the defendant pending her appeal to the Court of Appeal.

items.title: Form Two boy found drowned in Kuala Krai river, search continues for friend
items.summary: KUALA KRAI: One of two Form Two boys missing while swimming in a river near Kampung Aur Duri yesterday was found drowned this morning. The body of Lut Na'iman Mohd Noor Aziron, 14, was discovered at 9.10am by the Fire and Rescue Department Water Rescue Unit, about 40 minutes after the search and rescue operation resumed. Kuala Krai Fire and Rescue station chief Senior Fire Officer Nik Ahmad Afsham Nik Pa said the victim was found at a depth of three metres and 50 metres from where he was last seen.

items.title: Preschool teacher charged with sexual assault of 8-year-old pupil
items.summary: SEREMBAN: A preschool teacher was charged in the Sessions Court today with two counts of committing physical sexual assault against an 8-year-old male pupil in April. According to the two separate charges, the accused allegedly committed the acts inside a preschool classroom at a school in Rembau at 10am on April 1 and 9am on April 3. Deputy public prosecutor Nurul Balkis Zunaidi offered bail at RM20,000 with two additional conditions.

items.title: Aiman Athirah: Claims over Dengkil PPR's delay, safety, cost inaccurate
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The Housing and Local Government Ministry today dismissed allegations surrounding the Ampar Tenang People's Housing Project (PPR) in Dengkil, describing claims concerning safety, delays and infrastructure as inaccurate. Aiman Athirah, who also chairs the Task Force on Sick and Abandoned Private Housing Projects, said an emergency allocation of RM263,000 was approved for repairs. Addressing claims that the project had been delayed by up to 10 years, Aiman Athirah said PPR Ampar Tenang obtained its Certificate of Completion and Compliance (CCC) on Dec 31 under the current government.

items.title: Housewife charged with murder of 16-month-old step-granddaughter
items.summary: KOTA TINGGI: A 39-year-old housewife was charged in the Magistrate's Court here today for murdering her 16-month-old step-granddaughter last month. No plea was recorded from the accused, Nurul Farhana Laili Shah, who appeared before magistrate Hafizah Abdul Rajak. Yesterday, Johor police chief Datuk Ab Rahaman Arsad said the woman, who was the baby's step-grandmother, was arrested after the child was allegedly abused to death .

items.title: Johor housewife charged with murdering 16-month-old step-granddaughter in Kota Tinggi
items.summary: The accused, Nurul Farhana Laily Shah, indicated that she understood the charge after it was read before Magistrate Hafizah Abdul Rajak. However, no plea was recorded from the accused, who is also the victim’s step-grandmother, as the case falls under the jurisdiction of the High Court. According to the charge, Nurul Farhana is accused of murdering Nur Anggun Dahlia Abdullah between 12.30pm on July 30 and 9.30am on July 31 at a house along Jalan SS 6/13 in Taman Sri Saujana here.

items.title: Teleport strengthens Australia network through Avalon Airport
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Capital A Bhd's logistics arm, Teleport, has partnered with Avalon Airport Melbourne to establish a new strategic operations hub in Victoria, Australia. Through the agreement, Avalon Airport will serve as Teleport's latest Australian hub, supporting the movement of cargo and e-commerce shipments across key Asian trade routes and Australia through the airport's dedicated freight infrastructure. According to Teleport's CEO Pete Chareonwongsak, Avalon Airport is the right fit for Teleport's growth plans, as it delivers curfew-free capacity processing, fast turnarounds and the flexibility to handle eCommerce alongside general cargo.

items.title: Immigration dept caps Malaysian passport validity at 10 years after overseas travel issues, offers free replacement
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 12 — The Immigration Department has set the maximum validity period of the Malaysian International Passport (PMA) at 10 years with immediate effect, following issues faced by some Malaysian passport holders travelling overseas with passports valid for more than 10 years. Existing PMA holders with validity periods exceeding 10 years will be given free replacement passports, with the new passports having a maximum validity of 10 years. The department said affected PMA holders would also be given priority for passport replacement.

items.title: Kota Kinabalu airport security needs a closer look, Sabah rep says after string of overseas drug arrests
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Aug 12 — The relevant agencies have been called on to undertake a comprehensive security audit of Kota Kinabalu International Airport (KKIA). In making the call, Kapayan assemblyman Chin Teck Ming proposed that the review should include, among others, the adequacy of passenger screening procedures; baggage screening technology and detection capability; intelligence-led passenger risk assessment; as well as random and secondary screening procedures. Chin suggested the audit should also include staffing levels during operational hours; training and competency of screening personnel; coordination among all enforcement agencies operating at KKIA; and whether additional manpower, equipment, and technology are required to meet the highest international aviation security standards.

items.title: Sarawak Immigration detains 42 foreigners over suspected immigration offences
items.summary: KUCHING, Aug 12 — The Malaysian Immigration Department Sarawak has netted 42 foreigners suspected of committing various immigration offences. The operation followed complaints and intelligence gathered by the Kuching Immigration Enforcement Division to ensure compliance with immigration laws. Enforcement operations would continue to be intensified based on intelligence and public complaints received, said the department.

items.title: Malaysia and Australia eye domestic neodymium magnet production in rare earth push
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 12 — Malaysia and Australia are exploring closer cooperation in the rare earth elements (REE) and critical minerals sectors, including the development of domestic neodymium magnet manufacturing. It said Malaysia recognises Australia’s technical expertise and leadership in the critical minerals sector and is committed to developing a comprehensive domestic REE value chain, from midstream to downstream, in line with the National Mineral Policy 3 (NMP3). Apart from critical minerals, the ministry said both sides also discussed hazardous waste management, marine ecosystem conservation, climate financing and Malaysia’s commitment to the United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31).

items.title: Upko leader backs call for Sabah, Sarawak to secure one-third of parliamentary seats
items.summary: PENAMPANG, Aug 12 — United Progressive Kinabalu Organisation (Upko) Putatan division chief Jason Lee has backed the party president’s call for Sabah and Sarawak to be allocated no less than one-third of parliamentary seats as a constitutional safeguard. “We want Sabah’s voice to carry strength commensurate with Sabah’s position as one of the territories that formed Malaysia,” he said. They must understand Sabah’s rights.

items.title: JPJ to meet RXZ Members organisers over safety, improvements to motorcycle gathering
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 12 — The Road Transport Department (JPJ) will hold its first engagement session with RXZ Members organisers to discuss improvements to the motorcycle gathering, following a series of accidents linked to the event, Sinar Harian reported. JPJ Senior Director of Enforcement Datuk Muhammad Kifli Ma Hassan said the session aimed to hear the organisers’ views and propose several improvements to the programme. Muhammad Kifli said the engagement session would be held at the JPJ headquarters in Putrajaya today.

items.title: Legal action looms for Facebook page attacking Perak state developer
items.summary: IPOH, Aug 12 — The Perak State Development Corporation (PKNPk) has lodged reports with the police and the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) over the dissemination of various allegations against the corporation, its management and certain individuals linked to the organisation. In a statement, PKNPk said it was aware of several posts by a Facebook page which had recently been continuously publishing various serious allegations against PKNPk and its management. “In this regard, PKNPk lodged several reports and complaints with police and MCMC between July 30 and Aug 3 regarding the dissemination of the allegations,” the statement, posted on PKNPk’s official Facebook page, said.

items.title: Sarawak air quality stays unhealthy in nine areas as transboundary haze persists
items.summary: KUCHING, Aug 12 — The air quality in nine areas in Sarawak was at an unhealthy level as at 8 am today due to transboundary haze, compared with 11 areas yesterday morning. According to the Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS), Serian had an Air Pollutant Index reading of 194, Kuching (172), Samarahan (170), Sarikei (161), Bintulu (157), Sri Aman (157), Samalaju (152), Sibu (151) and Miri (133). API data is released hourly based on readings from 68 air quality monitoring stations nationwide.

items.title: Op Chick: MACC busts illegal China frozen chicken import ring in Sabah, three nabbed
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 12 — The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) has busted a syndicate suspected of illegally importing frozen chicken from China into Sabah by allegedly bribing authorities at a port, Sinar Harian reported. The operation was carried out by the MACC’s Intelligence Division in cooperation with the Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS) and the Royal Malaysian Customs Department. MACC chief commissioner Datuk Sri Abd Halim Aman confirmed the operation and arrests when contacted by Sinar Harian.

items.title: Taiwanese YouTuber targeted for foreign cash, 12 nabbed in RM35,000 Cheras robbery
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 12 — Police have arrested 12 Malaysians, including four women, over the alleged assault and robbery of a Taiwanese YouTuber at a condominium in Cheras, The Star reported last night. Kuala Lumpur police chief Datuk Fadil Marsus said police received a report from a Japanese man on Aug 1 over the incident, in which the Taiwanese victim was allegedly assaulted and robbed. Following the report, police launched a special operation involving the Cheras district police headquarters’ Criminal Investigation Division and the Kuala Lumpur Criminal Investigation Department.

items.title: All registered Malaysians in Colombia safe after 7.4-magnitude quake, says Wisma Putra
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 12 — The Foreign Ministry has confirmed that all registered Malaysians in Colombia are safe and accounted for following a powerful 7.4-magnitude earthquake that struck western Colombia on Monday. In a statement issued on Tuesday (Aug 11), the Foreign Ministry, also known as Wisma Putra, said the Embassy of Malaysia in Lima, Peru, which is concurrently accredited to Colombia, remains in close contact with the relevant local authorities and is closely monitoring developments. It advised Malaysians residing in or travelling to Colombia, particularly those in affected areas, to exercise utmost caution, remain vigilant, and comply with instructions and advisories issued by Colombian authorities and local emergency services.

items.title: Heritage pride, yes; public holiday, no: Melaka govt sets the record straight on Aug 21 despite Unesco heritage link
items.summary: MELAKA, Aug 12 — There will be no public holiday in Melaka on Aug 21, as the date is not listed in the state’s 2026 Public Holiday Schedule and no occasional holiday has been declared. State secretary Datuk Salhah Salleh said a clarification had been issued to dispel public confusion over Aug 21 (Friday), which has been linked to Melaka’s Unesco World Heritage recognition. At the same time, Salleh said the state government remained committed to preserving and promoting Melaka’s historical, cultural and heritage assets recognised as Unesco World Heritage Sites.

items.title: Perak police crack two cases: Armed robbery of Langkap woman, and Teluk Intan fishing shop break-in where one suspect is only 13
items.summary: IPOH, Aug 12 — A local man has been arrested for allegedly being involved in an armed robbery involving an elderly woman at a house in Langkap near Teluk Intan. Hilir Perak District Police chief ACP Chua Kok Lian said police received a report from the 69-year-old local woman, who claimed she had been robbed by an unidentified man. “Police also recovered and seized a gold bracelet believed to be linked to the case for further investigation,” he said in a statement last night.

items.title: Five Penang blackspots in police cross-agency push to clean up crime hotspots
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Aug 12 — Five blackspot areas in Penang have been identified as the focus of the 2026 Penang Police Contingent Whitening The Blackspot United For Safety Crime Prevention Initiative. State police chief Datuk Dennis Lim Kwang Keng said the initiative takes an integrated approach to tackling security, crime, social, infrastructure and environmental issues in the identified areas. “The initiative adopts a whole-of-government and whole-of-society approach that brings together the police, government agencies, local authorities, elected representatives, communities, non-governmental organisations, the private sector and strategic partners in a coordinated effort.

items.title: Finance Ministry: Tabung Haji’s finances are stronger, but taxpayers still bore the RM13b fallout
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 12 — Lembaga Tabung Haji’s (TH) current position is stable and increasingly stronger, following an increase in assets that exceed liabilities, depositors’ savings, and the distribution rate, said the Ministry of Finance (MOF). Emphasising the government’s full commitment to TH, the ministry said that the total assets of RM98.58 billion exceeded liabilities of RM95.63 billion as of Dec 31, 2025, while depositors’ savings rose from RM75.4 billion in 2018 to RM93.4 billion in 2025. “The distribution rate increased from 1.25 per cent in 2018 to 3.50 per cent in 2025, totalling RM3.22 billion,” it said.

items.title: Tabung Haji’s RM10b hole could have been avoided if BNM warnings were heeded, Dewan Rakyat told
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 12 — The financial crisis of Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) could have been avoided if the institution had taken appropriate action regarding warning letters concerning TH’s financial position, reserve levels, and liquidity management issued by Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM) since 2014. Minister in the Prime Department (Religious Affairs) Dr. Zulkifli Hasan said that based on records, BNM issued five warning letters to the TH Chairman and the responsible Minister between August 2014 and September 2016. Zulkifli said this when winding up debate at the Special Meeting of the Dewan Rakyat regarding the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) Report concerning TH in the Dewan Rakyat yesterday.

items.title: Tabung Haji’s RM27.5b UJSB sukuk safe, govt will honour guarantee, says Amir Hamzah
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 12 — The government always ensures that its debts are repaid, said Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan. He said government debt instruments such as Malaysian Government Securities (MGS) and Treasury bills, for example, are consistently serviced by the government. Amir Hamzah also explained that the government had restructured TH’s zero-coupon bond sukuk into sukuk with annual profit distributions to meet payment obligations for the RM27.5 billion sukuk issued by UJSB.

items.title: No Subang by-election, EC says after Wong Chen quits as MP
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 12 — The Election Commission of Malaysia (EC) has announced that a by-election (PRK) for the Subang parliamentary constituency will not be held following the resignation of its incumbent, Wong Chen, as the Member of Parliament. EC Chairman Datuk Seri Ramlan Harun said this is based on Article 54(1) of the Federal Constitution, as Dewan Rakyat Speaker Tan Sri Dr. Johari Abdul has informed the EC that there is no need to fill the vacancy. “No by-election for the P.104 Subang Parliamentary Constituency will be held,” he said in a statement last night.
